h: The New Fire Foreshadows the Lasting Repair of Creation

p: And it is further stated in Toras Kohanim (Toras Kohanim 31):
וַתֵּצֵא אֵשׁ מִלִּפְנֵי ה׳ (וַיִּקְרָא ט, כד)
"'And fire went forth from before Hashem' (Vayikra 9:24)
when they saw the new fire
to lick up on the Altar
רַק זָכַר שֶׁלֹּא כְּסֵדֶר הַכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה
only it mentions it not in the order written in the Torah:
and afterward "and they fell on their faces";
and we must understand why it changed it.
"And so in the days of Shlomo
the fire descend from heaven,' etc.,
'and they bowed with their faces to the ground,' etc.,
'and they prostrated themselves and gave thanks to Hashem,
for He is good, for His kindness is forever.'"
and afterward "and gave thanks to Hashem";
וְעַל אוֹתָהּ הַשָּׁעָה הוּא אוֹמֵר (מַלְאָכִי ג, ד)
'And the offering … shall be pleasing to Hashem,' etc.,
as in the days of Moshe
as in the days of Shlomo."
לָמָּה נִקְרָא יְמֵי מֹשֶׁה יְמֵי עוֹלָם
why the days of Moshe are called "days of old,"
and the days of Shlomo "former years."
And to say that Toras Kohanim expounded
"'As in the days of old' — as in the days of Noach;
as in the years of Hevel,
when there was no idolatry in the world";
and there Hevel came before Noach.
כִּימֵי מֹשֶׁה כִּימֵי שְׁלֹמֹה כִּימֵי נֹחַ
"as in the days of Moshe," "of Shlomo," "of Noach,"
but with Hevel, "as in the years of Hevel";
נִקְרָא יְמֵי מֹשֶׁה וְנֹחַ יְמֵי עוֹלָם
the days of Moshe and Noach are called "days of old,"
and those of Shlomo and Hevel "former years."
that Toras Kohanim was precise in its wording:
"and to lick up on the Altar
the olah and the fats," etc.
True, the pasuk is written so;
but why did it mention this
And also in the pasuk it says before (Vayikra 9:22):
"and he came down from offering the chatas
and the olah and the shelamim";
and it would have sufficed to write,
and consumed them on the Altar";
so why did the verse specify them in particular?
But an olah is entirely for Hashem,
and it is like offering one's soul before Hashem,
"They saw the ashes of Yitzchak," etc.,
though it was the ashes of the ram.
אַךְ הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
But it is according to what they said in the Midrash
"its sacrificial parts are as if they were Yitzchak's," etc.;
כְּאִלּוּ הִקְרַבְתִּי אֶת יִצְחָק בְּנִי תְּחִלָּה כוּ׳
"as if I had offered my son Yitzchak first," etc.
"Behold, I offered my soul before You";
for the offering of the ram
was like the offering of his soul.
And the chatas and the shelamim
only its fat and its blood," etc.;
"may my fat and my blood that have diminished," etc.
is like offering one's fat and blood.
Now at the Splitting of the Sea it is stated
(in the Mechilta and Midrash Rabbah, Beshalach)
that ruach hakodesh rested upon them
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ג סא, א)
that is, Chochmah, the supernal Kodesh.
and the Torah issues from Chochmah,
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ זוֹהַר חֵלֶק ב קכא, א)
"And wisdom — from where (me-ayin) shall it be found?"
that one becomes a chariot for the attribute of Ayin,
which is called the Holy of Holies,
(שָׁם סד, ב; וְאִדְרָא זוּטָא רפח, ב)
(Zohar II 64b; and Idra Zuta, Zohar III 288b).
And this is what prostration on the face indicates,
which is stretching out the hands and feet
that is, that one becomes as nothing.
that it would be so forever,
when he brought the holiness into all Yisrael,
so that they merited to see the new fire;
that is, as it will be in the future,
"And a new spirit I will put within you,"
and the yetzer hara will be cleared away
and as he said to them,
"Remove that yetzer hara from your heart"
And had he brought them into Eretz Yisrael,
it truly would have been so,
and he would have been Mashiach,
"That which was is that which will be"
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּתִּיקּוּנֵי זוֹהַר תִּיקּוּן יח, כו, א)
And this is what is said, "and they fell on their faces."
it was only for the moment,
for afterward the yetzer hara returned.
Therefore the verse put "and they sang out" first,
that their mouths were opened to sing the song;
but "and they fell on their faces"
this was only for the moment,
and it will be fulfilled in the future.
who merited all the lower wisdom in a dream
that is, from Hashem Yisbarach's side,
And in the utterance of Creation it is written (Bereishis 1:2):
זֶה רוּחוֹ שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ הַמָּשִׁיחַ כוּ׳
"This is the spirit of the King Mashiach," etc.;
who raised up the yoke of teshuvah
this is in the merit of teshuvah,
which comes through striving on man's part.
who merited wisdom in a dream,
for so was the will of the Creator,
And this is "upon the face of the waters,"
And this is what the holy Zohar alludes to
"All the fountains of the great deep were split open"
and he merited all of Torah she'b'al peh,
which is the Torah of Mashiach;
שֶׁכָּל מַה שֶּׁהָאָדָם לוֹמֵד בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה
for all that a person learns in this world
is vanity compared with the Torah of the World to Come
And when he brought this into all Yisrael,
that it would be so forever.
And this is what is said first:
"and they bowed with their faces to the ground," etc.;
that is, they became a chariot for the attribute of Ayin,
to make oneself as though one did not exist
וְאַחַר כָּךְ וְהוֹדוֹת לַה׳ כִּי טוֹב
and afterward "and gave thanks to Hashem, for He is good"
that is, "the light, that it was good" (Bereishis 1:4);
that it would be so forever.
it was not so for all time,
for that they will merit only in the future;
it was only for the moment.
Therefore it is called "the days of Shlomo"
to "as in the days of Moshe,"
and likewise "as in the days of Noach";
both are called "days of old" (olam, world):
for Noach was the only one in the world
who merited to see new fire;
and brought it to all Yisrael,
who are the sum of the entire world,
and the nations of the world are not counted;
therefore they are called "days of olam,"
for they were the sum of the entire world.

as is stated in Toras Kohanim (19):
that all the offerings had been brought," etc.,
"and the Shechinah had not descended to Yisrael,
My brother, so you have done to me,
that I went in and was put to shame," etc.;
וַיָּבֹא מֹשֶׁה וְאַהֲרֹן אֶל אֹהֶל מוֹעֵד
'And Moshe and Aharon went into the Ohel Moed,
and they came out and blessed the people.'"
That is, they brought the holiness
in the manner of what is said,
"And a new spirit I will put within you."
And it ascribed it to Moshe,
for it was because of him that Yisrael merited this,
when he went in with Aharon
And this is what is said before (Vayikra 9:22):
"And he came down from offering the chatas
and it is stated in Toras Kohanim (18):
he came down from the Altar in joy."
That is, according to what is said
who brought the Shechinah down to the earth;
to bring the holiness into the heart of Yisrael.
the bringing of holiness into the heart of Yisrael;
and therefore he came down from the Altar in joy.
to bring down the Holy One, blessed be He;
and when Moshe went in with Aharon,
"Behold, I offered my soul before You,"
this indicates that they rectified at the root
the serpent's blemish, which was in eating;
as on the first night of Pesach,
when they merited with the plague of the firstborn,
for the plague of the firstborn
therefore they merited then to eat the Pesach offering,
which is the eating of sacred offerings,
which indicates that the body is in holiness.
Therefore regarding Aharon it is written,
"and he came down from offering the chatas":
for on his part he merited
through the chatas and the olah;
so that he brings all Yisrael too to merit
and with this he came down in joy,
the Shechinah had not yet descended to Yisrael,
and when he went in with him,
for they brought the holiness into all of Yisrael.
"And fire went forth from before Hashem
and consumed on the Altar the olah"
to rectify the blemish at the root,
that they would eat in holiness.
Therefore it is written, "and they sang out,"
as it says, "Sing out, tzaddikim, in Hashem,"
and ruach hakodesh rested upon them
and afterward "and they fell on their faces,"
that one makes oneself as though one did not exist,
and they merit to become a chariot for the attribute of Ayin;
and this was for the moment,
and therefore they are called "days of old."
"'as in the days of old' — as in the days of Moshe,"
which was only for the moment;
and likewise "as in the days of Noach,"
which was certainly only for the moment;
as in the years of Hevel,
when there was no idolatry in the world";
for idolatry began in the days of Enosh,
And as long as there was no
although there was the yetzer hara,
it was within one's power to uproot the yetzer hara
as before the corruption of Adam HaRishon;
and therefore it is called "former years."
And it is called "the years of Hevel":
for though afterward he was killed
so that the new fire would be so forever,
over the matter of "and it was when they were in the field" (Bereishis 4:8),
nevertheless it is called "the years of Hevel,"
for all those years were fit
so that it would be "as in former years,"
כָּל זְמַן שֶׁלֹּא הָיָה הָעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה בָּעוֹלָם
as long as there was no idolatry in the world.
"and as in former years" about the days of Shlomo,
to rectify the whole root of the corruption,
so that it would be "former years,"
since he merited all the lower wisdom,
נִקְרָא בְּתוֹרַת כֹּהֲנִים רַק יְמֵי שְׁלֹמֹה
Toras Kohanim calls it only "the days of Shlomo"
only on the day the Beis HaMikdash was built,
וְעוֹד לֹא הָיוּ הַשָּׁנִים רְאוּיוֹת לְתִיקּוּן
and the years were not yet fit for rectification,
that will yet be in the future,
שֶׁיַּעֲשֶׂה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מָחוֹל לַצַּדִּיקִים
when the Holy One, blessed be He, will make a dance for the tzaddikim,
and each one will point with his finger (Taanis 31a);
for then there will truly be
"And a new spirit I will put within you,"
and it will be so, established for all time,
דְּיִתְפְּנֵי יֵצֶר הָרַע מִן תַּמָּן לְעוֹלָם
that the yetzer hara will be cleared from there forever;
